summary: cat prints a file, head prints the first lines, and tail prints the last lines. Use head and tail when a file is too long to read at once.
notes: head and tail show 10 lines unless you give -n with a number.
Log files add new lines at the bottom, so tail shows the most recent events.
For a long file you want to scroll through, use less (press q to quit). It does not run on this page because it waits for keys.
pitfall: cat on a folder fails with cat: cs: Is a directory. Use ls to see what is in a folder and cat to read a file.
